_meta.description: Legally verified against primary source text (Aug 2026) — each clause cites the specific Act section / circular number / paragraph it comes from, sourced via direct research against official/primary documents (DPDP Act bare text, RBI circulars fetched from rbi.org.in, CERT-In Directions fetched from cert-in.org.in, SEBI/IRDAI circulars triangulated across 3+ independent secondary sources where the primary PDF was not machine-readable). Corrections were made to 6 of 19 clauses where the original paraphrase overstated scope or misattributed a source; caveats were added where a clause's legal force, applicability, or citation confidence is not simple 'currently binding as written'.
_meta.known_limitations: SEBI and IRDAI circular PDFs returned as non-extractable/scanned content — those 5 clauses are verified via convergent secondary sources (law-firm client alerts, compliance vendors), not a direct primary-text read, and are flagged individually where a specific clause/paragraph number could not be confirmed.

clauses.summary: Under Section 6(1), consent — and therefore processing — must be limited to personal data necessary for the specified purpose; under Section 8(7), the fiduciary must erase the data once that purpose is no longer being served, unless retention is legally required.
clauses.caveat: Enacted Aug 2023, but this substantive provision is not yet in force — commencement is phased and this section takes effect 14 May 2027 per MeitY's notification; only definitions and Data Protection Board setup provisions are currently operative.

clauses.summary: Section 16(1) allows the Central Government to notify that transfer of personal data to specified countries/territories outside India is restricted; absent such a notification, cross-border transfer is permitted by default.
clauses.caveat: Enacted Aug 2023, not yet in force — effective 14 May 2027. As of this writing, no country/territory restriction has actually been notified under this section.

clauses.summary: Any third-party service that processes personal data on a company's behalf is a Data Processor, and the company (as Data Fiduciary) remains accountable for that processor's handling of the data, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary.
clauses.caveat: Enacted Aug 2023, not yet in force — effective 14 May 2027.

clauses.summary: Under Section 8(6), a Data Fiduciary must intimate the Data Protection Board and each affected Data Principal of a personal data breach in the form/manner prescribed by rules; Rule 7 of the DPDP Rules, 2025 specifies this must happen without delay, with a detailed report to the Board within 72 hours.
clauses.caveat: Enacted, not yet in force — effective 14 May 2027; Rule 7's 72-hour detail is likewise not yet operative.

clauses.framework: RBI Cyber Security Framework (Scheduled Commercial Banks)
clauses.summary: RBI's Cyber Security Framework circular requires time-bound, need-to-know access provisioning, deactivation of dormant accounts, and ongoing oversight of vendor arrangements — a synthesis of several baseline controls rather than one named 'periodic access review' clause.
clauses.caveat: Applies specifically to Scheduled Commercial Banks (excluding RRBs) — NOT cooperative banks (separate framework: DCBS.CO.PCB.Cir.No.1/18.01.000/2018-19) or NBFCs (separate Master Direction). Citing this against a cooperative-bank tenant is a category error.

clauses.framework: RBI Cyber Security Framework (Scheduled Commercial Banks)
clauses.summary: Banks must evaluate and select vendors based on comprehensive risk assessment before onboarding, conduct background checks on vendor/third-party personnel, and continue regular due diligence and oversight afterward — not only periodic review after the fact.
clauses.caveat: Applies specifically to Scheduled Commercial Banks (excluding RRBs) — NOT cooperative banks or NBFCs, which have separate frameworks.

clauses.summary: RBI's April 2018 circular requires payment system data to be stored only in India, permitting foreign-leg transaction data to also be stored abroad; the specific 24-hours-or-1-business-day (whichever earlier) deletion requirement for such foreign-stored data comes from RBI's subsequent FAQ clarification of June 2019, not the original circular itself.
clauses.citation: RBI/2017-18/153, DPSS.CO.OD No.2785/06.08.005/2017-18 (6 Apr 2018); RBI FAQ clarification (26 Jun 2019)

clauses.summary: Only the 20 specific categories of cyber security incidents listed in Annexure I (e.g. data breach, data leak, ransomware, unauthorized access, DDoS, phishing) must be reported to CERT-In within 6 hours of the entity noticing the incident or being notified of it — not all cyber incidents generally.
clauses.citation: CERT-In Directions No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In (28 Apr 2022), para (ii) & Annexure I
clauses.caveat: In force since 27 Jun 2022 and currently binding, but its constitutional validity is under a pending, unresolved challenge in the Delhi High Court.

clauses.summary: Access grants should be scoped to the minimum permission level needed, and should be revoked when a tool becomes dormant or is no longer needed for its original purpose.

SEBI's CSCRF classifies regulated entities into five tiers — Market Infrastructure Institutions, Qualified REs, Mid-size REs, Small-size REs, and Self-certification REs — with third-party/vendor risk-assessment rigor (e.g. cyber-resilience audits) scaling by tier rather than simply by size.

Critical/core systems must maintain a Software Bill of Materials covering all software types (in-house, third-party custom, COTS, open-source, SaaS) with fields including license, supplier, transitive dependencies, and cryptographic hashes; legacy systems unable to comply need a board-approved risk-mitigation plan instead.
clauses.citation: SEBI/HO/ITD-1/ITD_CSC_EXT/P/CIR/2024/113 (exact clause/paragraph number not independently confirmed — primary PDF was not machine-readable; substance corroborated across 6+ independent compliance-vendor sources)

clauses.summary: Insurers and insurance intermediaries (brokers, corporate agents, web aggregators, TPAs, IMFs, repositories, and others) must manage third-party/vendor risk under a board-approved cybersecurity policy, with VAPT at least twice yearly and critical findings remediated within 30 days.

IRDAI's 2023 Cyber Security Guidelines exempt insurers from that guideline's own data-localization clause (it applies to "Regulated Entities other than insurers"); insurers' actual policyholder-data localization duty instead sits in separate instruments (the Maintenance of Insurance Records Regulations 2015, e-commerce guidelines, and Minimum Information Regulations 2020).
clauses.citation: IRDAI/GA&HR/GDL/MISC/88/04/2023; IRDAI (Maintenance of Insurance Records) Regulations, 2015
clauses.caveat: The commonly-cited 6-hour incident-reporting figure for policyholder data has only single-source confirmation in this research pass — treat as lower-confidence pending further check.

clauses.summary: Consent for processing personal data must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous, given through clear affirmative action, and must be as easily withdrawable as it was to give.
clauses.caveat: Enacted Aug 2023, not yet in force — effective 14 May 2027.

clauses.summary: A Significant Data Fiduciary (as notified by the government) must appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India reporting to the board of directors, appoint an independent data auditor, and undertake periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments and audits.
clauses.caveat: Enacted Aug 2023, not yet in force — effective 14 May 2027.

clauses.summary: Failure to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach (Section 8(5)) can attract a penalty of up to two hundred fifty crore rupees under Item 1 of the Act's penalty Schedule; separately, failure to notify a breach under Section 8(6) carries a distinct, lower ceiling of two hundred crore rupees.
clauses.caveat: Enacted Aug 2023, not yet in force — effective 14 May 2027.

clauses.summary: Organizations must enable and securely maintain logs of their ICT systems for a rolling 180 days, within Indian jurisdiction, and provide them to CERT-In on request.
clauses.caveat: In force since 27 Jun 2022 and currently binding, but its constitutional validity is under a pending, unresolved challenge in the Delhi High Court.

clauses.summary: Data centres, VPS, cloud service, and VPN service providers must register and maintain 7 specific subscriber data fields (validated name, hire period, allotted IPs, registration email/IP/timestamp, purpose, address/contact, ownership pattern) for 5 years after registration cancellation or withdrawal.
clauses.caveat: In force since 27 Jun 2022 and currently binding, but its constitutional validity is under a pending, unresolved challenge in the Delhi High Court.

clauses.summary: SEBI-regulated entities must report cybersecurity incidents to SEBI and CERT-In within 6 hours of detection (with a separate 30-minute window to declare a "Disaster" for critical-system disruption), and maintain an incident response plan tiered to the entity's CSCRF classification.
